content:
You can be in South Carolina in under five minutes from downtown Augusta — the state line runs right through the middle of the Savannah River. That geography is the whole reason South Carolina day trips from Augusta are so easy to pull off: you're not committing to a weekend, you're just crossing a bridge. Whether you want a half-day in Aiken, a full day in Columbia, or a long haul to Charleston, here's the honest breakdown of what's worth the drive — plus where to stay when you get back.

Why Augusta Is the Best Base for South Carolina Day Trips

Augusta sits on the west bank of the Savannah River, directly across from North Augusta, South Carolina. From downtown — Broad Street, the Riverwalk, the Augusta Common — you're minutes from the state line. That means South Carolina day trips from Augusta don't eat your whole day in transit the way they would from Atlanta or Athens.

The other advantage: Augusta has far more lodging capacity than any of the small South Carolina towns within an hour's drive. Aiken and North Augusta have charming downtowns but limited hotels. Staying in Augusta and day-tripping out gives you the best of both — a real city to come home to, and small-town South Carolina to explore.

1. Aiken, SC — The Closest True Day Trip

Drive time from Augusta: about 30 minutes via US-78 or SC-19.

Aiken is the quintessential South Carolina day trip from Augusta — close enough for a spontaneous afternoon, distinct enough to feel like a real escape. The draw is the equestrian culture (Aiken is a winter training hub for thoroughbreds), the Hitchcock Woods (one of the largest urban forests in the country, with 70+ miles of trails), and a walkable downtown along Laurens Street and Richland Avenue.

What to actually do in Aiken

  • Walk or ride the trails in Hitchcock Woods — free, open daily, and genuinely beautiful in fall.
  • Browse Laurens Street and Richland Avenue for boutiques, antique shops, and coffee.
  • Tour the Aiken Thoroughbred Racing Hall of Fame in Hopelands Gardens.
  • Time your visit for a steeplechase or polo match if you can — Aiken's equestrian calendar runs fall through spring.

This is the day trip to take if you've got a half-day free and don't want to spend it in the car.

2. North Augusta & the Greenway — The Five-Minute Day Trip

Drive time from Augusta: 5–10 minutes across the 13th Street or Calhoun Expressway bridges.

North Augusta is technically a separate city in a separate state, but it functions as an extension of Augusta — and it's home to the North Augusta Greeneway, a paved trail network that's excellent for cycling and walking. The Riverside Village area has restaurants and riverfront access, and the Living History Park is a free, genuinely interesting stop if you're traveling with kids.

This isn't a full-day trip, but it's the perfect add-on to a morning on the Augusta Riverwalk — cross the bridge, ride the Greeneway, come back for lunch.

3. Edgefield, SC — Small-Town History and Pottery

Drive time from Augusta: about 45 minutes via SC-28.

Edgefield is one of those South Carolina towns that punches above its weight. It's the birthplace of ten South Carolina governors, has a well-preserved downtown square, and is a serious destination for pottery — Edgefield stoneware is collected nationally, and several working potteries still operate in the area. The National Wild Turkey Federation headquarters is here too, with a free museum that's better than it sounds.

Go for a half-day, hit the square, and stop at a pottery studio on the way out.

4. Columbia, SC — The Full-Day Capital Trip

Drive time from Augusta: about 1 hour 15 minutes via I-20 East.

Columbia is the biggest South Carolina day trip from Augusta that still fits in a single day. The Riverbanks Zoo & Garden is one of the best zoos in the Southeast, the South Carolina State Museum is excellent for families, and the Vista and Five Points districts have real restaurant and bar scenes. If you're here during college football season, a Gamecocks game at Williams-Brice Stadium is a genuine experience.

Columbia tips

  • Park once in the Vista and walk — downtown Columbia is more walkable than it looks.
  • Riverbanks Zoo is best on a weekday morning; weekends get crowded by 11 a.m.
  • If you're combining Columbia with a Masters Week trip, do Columbia on a practice-round day and save the tournament days for Augusta.

5. Charleston & the Coast — The Long-Haul Day Trip

Drive time from Augusta: about 2 hours 45 minutes to Charleston via I-20 and I-26; about 2 hours 30 minutes to Beaufort; about 3 hours to Hilton Head.

Charleston is doable as a day trip from Augusta, but it's a long one — you'll want to leave early and accept that you're getting a taste, not a full visit. The payoff is real: the French Quarter, King Street, the Waterfront Park pineapple fountain, and She Crab Soup at any of a dozen places. If you're going to do it, go on a weekday and skip July and August heat.

Beaufort is the smarter long-haul day trip if you want Lowcountry without the Charleston crowds — smaller, quieter, and about 30 minutes closer.

6. Savannah, GA — The Cross-Border Classic

Drive time from Augusta: about 2 hours 15 minutes via US-25 or I-20/I-95.

Technically Georgia, not South Carolina — but Savannah is the day trip most Augusta visitors actually take, and it belongs on this list. The Historic District, Forsyth Park, River Street, and the food scene are worth the drive. Go early, park once near Forsyth Park, and walk.

Where to Stay in Augusta for South Carolina Day Trips

Here's the thing most visitors get wrong: they book a downtown Augusta hotel, fight for parking every night, and spend their mornings sitting in traffic on Broad Street or Washington Road. Planning Your South Carolina Day Trips: A Quick Reference

  • Half-day: Aiken, North Augusta Greeneway, Edgefield.
  • Full day: Columbia, Beaufort, Savannah.
  • Long day (leave early): Charleston, Hilton Head.
  • Zero-drive option: kayak the Savannah River from KJ's private dock — six kayaks included, no trailer, no rental counter.

One practical note: if you're visiting during Masters Week, book your South Carolina day trips around the tournament schedule, not the other way around. Practice rounds (Monday–Wednesday) are the best days to be out of town; tournament days are the best days to be at the course. And if you're staying at KJ, use the private back route to Augusta National — it's the difference between a 15-minute drive and an hour in Masters traffic.
